source.title: DataShield: Uncovering Risky Fine-Tuning Data Across LLMs Through Consensus Subspace Alignment
source.authors: Ze-Feng Wu; Wei-Wei Qi; Jie Chen; Tian-Hang Zheng; Di Hong; Chao-Chao Lu; Liang He; Zhan Qin; Kui Ren

record.tranche_reason: Tests ordinary supervised fine-tuning on instruction data and harmful-request ASR on target models, using the same broad fine-tuning-and-safety-measure setup as the cited claim, but in different datasets and model settings.
record.gate_note: The paper explicitly says standard SFT on both datasets causes clear safety degradation. Table 1 reports ASR after standard SFT, but does not give numeric pre-fine-tuning ASR values. Other DataShield filtering and masking results concern the paper's proposed intervention, not the claim versions. Layer-perturbation results are used only to choose safety-critical layers and are not extracted as rows.
record.test_reason: The Standard SFT baseline fine-tunes four safety-aligned instruct models on Alpaca and Dolly (safety-related examples removed) and reports harmful-request ASR on HEx-PHI and HarmBench. This is the same benign-data recipe and benchmark family as Qi et al., and the authors state it causes clear safety degradation.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that benign downstream SFT degrades safety. They find that DataShield's cross-model consensus-subspace filtering or segment masking lowers ASR more than baselines while largely preserving utility.
record.recipe_differences: Tests standard downstream SFT on Alpaca and Dolly using LoRA and harmful-request ASR, rather than a small-data fine-tuning sweep; the original source's exact recipe is not stated in this paper.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that outcomes vary with source-model choice, subspace dimensionality, intervention budget, segment splitter, pooling rule, and source-score aggregation; these are sensitivities of DataShield, not of the ordinary-SFT result rows.
record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: The standard-SFT table does not report numerical pre-fine-tuning ASR baselines, limiting direct quantification of the increase. Results are averaged over multiple random-seed runs, but no error bars, confidence intervals, standard deviations, or p-values are stated here.
record.rows_left_out: No directly relevant results omitted. DataShield and baseline filtering/masking outcomes are not rows for the claim versions; the layer-perturbation plots are used only for layer selection.

untested.parts: Carefully chosen or outlier benign subsets and a data-quantity sweep are untested. Pre-fine-tuning ASR is never reported numerically, so the size of the increase cannot be computed.
No per-token KL or position analysis.
No prefilling, suffix or decoding attacks.
Layer-perturbation refusal sensitivity is used only to pick layers for scoring. No test that a few weights carry safety.
Not tested. DataShield is data filtering, not deepening of alignment.

missing.what: Standard full-parameter fine-tuning baseline ASR on Alpaca and Dolly for Qwen3-4B, Qwen2.5-14B and Gemma3-12B (PHI 25.8–42.5%, HARM 32.5–50.8%).
Standard SFT ASR re-judged by Gemini-3.1-pro for Phi3 and Qwen3 (e.g., Phi3 Dolly HARM 77.5, Qwen3 Alpaca PHI 33.6).

Random-Sp (benign fine-tuning on a random 80% of the data) on CodeAlpaca gives ASR 28–58%. On MathInstruct ASR is only 1.7–11.4%, suggesting dataset-dependent erosion. No unfiltered SFT or pre-fine-tuning baseline is reported.
Random-Sp and Random-Sm benign fine-tuning ASR on Qwen2.5-72B and Llama3-70B with Dolly (Llama3-70B HARM 64.8–69.2%).

record.verdict_notes: All rows' 'observed' state rests on the authors' statement plus high absolute ASR, since no pre-fine-tuning ASR is reported. SLM utility is a win rate against the pre-fine-tuning model, not a safety baseline. The MathInstruct results (Random-Sp, low ASR) hint that the erosion depends on the dataset. That would bear on V2's scope, but there is no unfiltered baseline, so no label is given. The paper is a mitigation study; its DataShield and baseline-filter results are correctly excluded from the rows.

versions.untested_parts: Harmful-data fine-tuning and the effect of a few to a few hundred harmful examples are not tested.
The paper tests ordinary instruction data, but not carefully selected benign examples or a small-data quantity sweep.
Per-token KL divergence between aligned and base models is not measured.
Prefilled compliant openings, suffixes, and decoding changes are not tested.
The paper's layer-sensitivity analysis is used to select layers; it does not test whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behaviour.
The cause of first-token or other safety shallowness is not tested.
Training to deepen safety across response positions and its robustness are not tested.

relation.reason: The study reports ordinary-SFT harmful-request ASR and explicitly states that standard SFT degrades safety on both datasets.

tranche.reason: Standard benign-data supervised fine-tuning and harmful-request compliance evaluation match the original V2 method and measure.

source_check.notes: Table 1's extracted dataset labels are misleading: Section 5.2 identifies the 76.0% block as Alpaca, while Table 2 independently identifies the 78.5% block as Dolly. Observed states rely on the authors' explicit degradation statement; post-tuning ASR alone does not quantify an increase.

statements.correction: Phi3-medium Standard SFT: Alpaca HEx-PHI 62.0%, HarmBench 76.0%; Dolly HEx-PHI 64.5%, HarmBench 78.5%. Numerical pre-tuning safety ASR not stated. Reviewed publication status not established in supplied text.
statements.problem: The Phi3-medium percentages belong to Alpaca, not Dolly. Missing numerical untreated safety baselines is correctly described. The supplied text does not establish the claimed reviewed venue.
